Diagnosis: set_key (main.py:184-185) escapes only apostrophes when single-quoting, leaving literal backslashes raw. The parser (parser.py:25,32,132) decodes `\\` and `\'` in single-quoted values, so raw backslashes are misinterpreted (`\n`→newline, `\\`→`\`, trailing `\` breaks parsing). Round-trip fails for any backslash.

Plan: In set_key's quoting branch, escape backslashes before apostrophes: `value_out = "'{}'".format(value_to_set.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'"))`. Backslash-first ordering avoids double-escaping. This aligns with the parser's single-quote escape set, preserving always/auto/never modes and export behavior; no parser changes needed. Verify via dotenv_values(interpolate=False) with values containing `\`, `\\`, `\'`, and trailing backslashes.
